items.evidence: All four labware loaded with the right load names, slots and labels; p20 left and p300 right with the correct tip racks in slots 10 and 11.
Each of the 96 wells gets p20.aspirate(18, mm['A1']) then dispense(18, well). The end_state:pcr_plate check passed.
1 µL aspirated from colony[w.well_name] and dispensed into the matching PCR well, then p20.mix(3, 10, w). The end-state checks passed.
1 µL primer is transferred from primers[w.well_name] to the matching PCR well, giving 18+1+1 = 20 µL. The pcr_plate end-state check passed.

Colony and primer steps use a fresh tip per well, and no_cross_contamination passed. Master mix reuses one tip across all 96 wells, which is acceptable since the wells are empty and the tip only touches reagent, but the tip is dispensed into the wells without contact control.
protocol.comment records the sealing step and the full program: 98C 30 s; 30 cycles of 98C 10 s, 60C 30 s, 72C 30 s; 72C 2 min; hold 4C.

1 µL steps are on the p20 as intended, but dispensing uses default heights with no touch tip or blow-out. The mix volume of 10 µL in a 2 µL-liquid well is wasteful and the mix is the only mixing. Master mix is done with 96 individual 18 µL aspirations, which is acceptable.
The protocol follows the task steps and order with an accurate thermocycling comment. Nothing is invented.

judge.summary: The protocol meets the specified deck, volumes, order and thermocycling comment, and all measured checks passed. Minor practice weaknesses are the single shared tip for the master mix, default pipetting heights and flow, and a 10 µL mix volume in a well holding about 20 µL.
